title: Bauhaus Design Principles in Motion
subtitle: Explainer video
line: An explainer that teaches Bauhaus principles by moving like them: geometry, primary colour and rhythm, animated with a four-person team.
desc: Driven by a collective desire to infuse innovation into our craft, we embarked on a journey to marry the fluidity of motion with the structured elegance of Bauhaus design. The result is an explainer that teaches the principles by demonstrating them: every transition, easing curve and colour block is doing the teaching.
details: Storyboard: Tolu Aina
Animation: Stanley Agoha and Tolu Aina
Illustration: Mercy Ajiboye
Sound design: Gregory Henry
Creative direction: Stanley Agoha
challenge: Explain a design movement built on restraint without the film itself becoming static. The storyboard had to find motion inside geometry that was designed to sit still.
solution: Treated each Bauhaus principle as a rule for how the shapes may move: circles roll, squares slide on a grid, triangles pivot from a point. The rhythm came from the sound design, which was cut before the final animation pass.

title: Perspective
subtitle: Ravie.co motion design challenge
line: Four vertical loops that push flat shapes into depth: a ramp, a column, a wave, a grid. Made for the Ravie.co Perspective challenge.
desc: A Ravie.co challenge on the theme of perspective, made with Nicholas Candeias, Stephanie Kubudi Cardeman and OneMoreDay. Each piece takes a flat, Illustrator-built composition and gives it depth in After Effects: shapes recede along a grid, a column twists in space, a circle opens into a tunnel. Built entirely in 2D tools, which was the point.
details: Collaborators: Nicholas Candeias, Stephanie Kubudi Cardeman, OneMoreDay
Four 9:16 loops for vertical screens
Palette: 100B1F · 1F4CBC · FF4A11 · FFB111 · FFFFFD
All depth faked in After Effects with 2D layers, parallax and gradient ramps
challenge: Make flat graphics read as three-dimensional without a 3D package, and keep four separate pieces feeling like one set.
solution: One palette, one grid and one camera language across all four. Depth comes from overlap, scale and gradient direction, so the pieces stay crisp at any resolution and cheap to render.

title: Step Forward
subtitle: 3D motion spot for a Converse-style shoe
line: A 15-second spec ad built in Blender and After Effects: a sneaker in a minimal 3D space with orbiting type. Built to move, made to last.
desc: A short, visually engaging shoe advertisement that uses 3D animation to highlight the shoe's unique features. The aim was to blend motion design, product visualisation and sound design into a compelling 15 to 30 second piece. Modelled and rendered in Blender (Cycles), finished in After Effects.
details: Visual style: sleek, minimalistic 3D environment with orbiting text
Colour palette: monochrome with a blue brand accent
Mood: futuristic, luxurious, streetwear
Typography: bold sans-serif, high contrast, clean motion curves
Sound design: RnB, laid back, sentimental (music: Freepik, High Rise)
Creative direction, design and animation: Tolu Aina

title: The Rubik's Cube Experiment
subtitle: 10-second light study
line: A Rubik's cube stripped of colour and given light instead. One cube, one camera move, a purple and pink room. Personal project.
desc: This started as a simple question: what happens when you strip a Rubik's cube of its colour and give it light instead? A personal motion design project, a 10-second video built around a glowing 3D cube, dynamic camera movement, and a deep purple and pink environment. No rules, no brief, just a shape and an idea. The goal was to push my understanding of light behaviour in 3D and explore how much life you can give a single object through glow, environment and motion alone.
details: The sketch: six rough panels mapping the motion. It starts on a light source, moves into the cube appearing and rotating, and closes back on the light. Kept simple on purpose.
The styleframes were red. The finish is white and purple. That shift happened in the process, and that is exactly the point.

desc: A three-second vertical loop made for the sake of making it: a retro controller, a blue room and one move. Experiments like this are where the timing gets tested before it ends up in client work.

title: uLesson explainers
line: 100+ animated lessons for one of West Africa's largest edtech apps. Four samples inside, each playable.
subtitle: Educational animation at scale
desc: uLesson teaches the school curriculum to millions of students across West Africa through short animated lessons. Across two stints, first as a motion graphic designer and later as senior animator, I made over a hundred of them: character-driven story scenes like this one, diagram-led explainers for maths and science, and the lower thirds, transitions and templates that kept a 20-plus person animation team consistent as it scaled. The four samples above are English lessons, told as stories rather than lectures, which is how uLesson keeps young students watching to the end.
details: 100+ explainer and lesson videos across English, maths and science, contributing to a 20% increase in app downloads
Helped set the visual consistency standards for a rapidly scaling animation team of 20+
Built the lower-thirds, transition and template systems in After Effects and Illustrator that the team produced from
Worked with R&D on AI-assisted production that cut time and cost by 30% without dropping quality
Motion graphics for marketing campaigns that lifted user engagement by 15%
challenge: Volume without sameness. Hundreds of lessons a year, each needing to feel made for its subject, on a schedule that left no room for reworking scenes.
solution: Systems first: a character and background library, template rigs for recurring devices (lower thirds, callouts, diagrams), and a review rhythm that caught problems at the animatic stage rather than in render. That is what made a hundred-plus videos possible without the quality sliding.
videosLabel: Four lessons. Each plays on its own; press one, then the next.

title: Pepsi MAX UK campaign
subtitle: Platform-specific video suite from one key visual
line: Four cuts from one Pepsi key visual: a motion poster, two Instagram Stories and a TikTok native, each paced for where it plays. Client work, 2023.
desc: A series of clean, animated brand visuals built from the core key visual, combining smooth motion, controlled transitions and precise timing to create a polished, platform-ready set of digital video assets. Pepsi needed video for several platforms that kept one visual identity and one clear message across every format.
details: Motion poster: animated the lead key visual to feel like a static billboard brought to life
Social video: staggered three messages, opening on a human moment before moving to product, with a vertical scroll that mimics a live feed
Bumper: adapted the vertical structure into a forced-view format built to grab attention and hold it for the full runtime
TikTok: stripped the branding back for a short, native-feeling execution aligned with how the platform behaves
challenge: Keep brand consistency across formats while adapting motion, pacing and layout to each platform, with every brand detail aligned precisely so transitions and animation feel smooth and intentional.
solution: One key visual, one motion language, four deliveries. Delivered a cohesive multi-platform video suite that respected Pepsi brand guidelines while optimising each asset for its audience and viewing context.
videosLabel: Four deliverables. Each plays on its own.

title: Swiffer Instagram Stories
subtitle: Four 9:16 cuts for a duster launch
line: Four Instagram Stories for Swiffer: live-action edits with brand end cards, and macro animation of dust and hair caught in the fibres. Studio work, 2023.
desc: A set of Instagram Stories for Swiffer, built for the vertical feed. Two cuts edit live-action footage down to a single beat and land on the brand end card. The other two go macro: an animated close-up of the duster's fibres trapping dust, pollen and hair, painted rather than rendered, so the product demo reads as texture instead of a diagram.
details: Four 9:16 cuts, sized and paced for Instagram Stories
Live-action edit to end card: one message, one beat, logo
Macro animation of dust and hair caught in the fibres, built in After Effects from painted layers
Brand colour system (green, yellow, orange) held across live and animated cuts
challenge: Make a duster interesting for the three seconds a Stories viewer gives you, and make the animated demo feel like the same campaign as the live-action.
solution: Lead with the person, close with the product. The macro cuts borrow the live footage's palette and lighting so the switch from film to animation reads as a zoom, not a change of world.
videosLabel: Four Stories. Each plays on its own.
